lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the modern narrow Scrophulariaceae rather than the old broad 'everything with a bilabiate flower' family.

project_scope.note: Modern molecular classification removed many traditional scrophs into Plantaginaceae, Orobanchaceae, Paulowniaceae and other Lamiales families. The learner must not use old broad-family membership uncritically.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with a fused 4–5-lobed corolla and a superior usually 2-carpellate ovary, then inspect stamen number and fruit. Modern Scrophulariaceae commonly has 2–4(–5) epipetalous stamens and a capsule, but the family is diverse.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs, shrubs or small trees. Leaves simple, alternate/opposite/whorled; stipules generally absent. Hairs may be woolly or glandular.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual, regular to strongly zygomorphic; calyx 4–5-lobed; corolla fused; stamens usually 2 or 4, sometimes 5; ovary superior and commonly 2-locular with axile placentation.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a septicidal or loculicidal capsule, less often berry/drupelike.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Do not identify 'Scrophulariaceae' from a bilabiate corolla alone. Modern family recognition depends on the genus door plus superior ovary/capsule and exclusion of neighboring Lamiales families. Genus check: Verbascum thapsus has five stamens, commonly three with hairy filaments and two longer nearly hairless; Leucophyllum has four fertile stamens. Do not use four stamens as universal for this family.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: modern-family warning → superior ovary/capsule → three project genus doors → Plantaginaceae/Orobanchaceae/Paulowniaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Scrophulariaceae is a taxonomy lesson as much as a morphology lesson. Many plants once called figwort family are now elsewhere, so the local genera matter.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the modern-family warning
steps.look_for: Buddleja, Leucophyllum and Verbascum remain here; many familiar old 'scrophs' such as Penstemon are now in Plantaginaceae.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents old field-guide family labels from becoming permanent misconceptions.

steps.title: 2 · Buddleja door: small clustered flowers on a Texas shrub
steps.photo_role: Buddleja racemosa leaf node + flower cluster
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves on a shrub and many small 4-merous tubular flowers clustered along the inflorescence.
steps.why_it_matters: Buddleja is a woody Scrophulariaceae form and a strong Edwards Plateau project anchor.

steps.title: 3 · Leucophyllum door: silver leaves + purple axillary flowers
steps.look_for: Dense silvery stellate hairs on opposite leaves and showy purple-pink tubular flowers arising from leaf axils.
steps.why_it_matters: The silver-foliage shrub architecture is instantly recognizable once tied to the family.

steps.title: 4 · Verbascum door: woolly rosette + yellow spike
steps.look_for: Large woolly basal leaves and a tall spike of yellow 5-part flowers; capsule remains after flowering.
steps.why_it_matters: It is the herbaceous extreme of the project family and an introduced comparison.

steps.title: 5 · Confirm the superior capsule
steps.look_for: Ovary above the other floral whorls, commonly 2-locular and maturing into a dry capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Helps split Scrophulariaceae from inferior-ovary Lamiales lookalikes.

comparisons.title: Scrophulariaceae vs Plantaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Flower shape overlaps heavily. Use current genus placement plus fruit/stamen details; Penstemon and many old snapdragon relatives are Plantaginaceae, not modern Scrophulariaceae.

comparisons.title: Scrophulariaceae vs Orobanchaceae
comparisons.rule: Orobanchaceae is defined by parasitism/haustoria and includes green hemiparasites; project Scrophulariaceae is autotrophic.

comparisons.title: Scrophulariaceae vs Paulowniaceae
comparisons.rule: Paulownia is now a separate family: large opposite cordate leaves, tree habit and woody capsules packed with winged seeds.

visual_lesson.caveat: Modern Scrophulariaceae is not safely keyed from one universal visible feature. Use genus identity plus the family-level superior-ovary/capsule pattern and current taxonomy.
